Hand off spatial objects to tmap, leaflet and friends

geo-map-interop.Rd

tidymapr keeps mapping in ggplot via plot_sites(), plot_geo() and plot_topo(), but never blocks tmap, leaflet or other spatial viewers. These helpers return plain sf and terra objects (with a CRS) so tmap::tm_shape(), leaflet::addTiles(), leaflet::addCircleMarkers() and leaflet::addRasterImage() work without extra wrangling. Neither tmap nor leaflet is a hard Import; examples are wrapped in requireNamespace().

Usage

as_sf(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_sf(x, lon = lon, lat = lat, crs = 4326, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sf'
as_sf(x, crs = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tmr_geo_sf'
as_sf(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tmr_sdm'
as_sf(x, ...)

as_spat_raster(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_spat_raster(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
as_spat_raster(x, crs = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
as_spat_raster(x, lon = lon, lat = lat, value = NULL, crs = "EPSG:4326", ...)

# S3 method for class 'tmr_sdm'
as_spat_raster(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A data frame with coordinates, an sf object, a SpatRaster, a tmr_sdm prediction tibble, or another supported spatial result.

...

Passed to geo_as_sf() or ignored.

lon, lat

Coordinate columns when x is a data frame.

crs

Target CRS (default EPSG:4326).

value

Column to place in a single-layer SpatRaster when converting a point table with a numeric attribute (optional).

Value

as_sf() returns an sf object (subclass tmr_geo_sf when built from coordinates). as_spat_raster() returns a terra::SpatRaster with a CRS.

Examples

sites <- geo_example_sites()
sites <- sites[!is.na(sites$lon), ]
pts <- as_sf(sites)
inherits(pts, "sf")
#> [1] TRUE
sf::st_crs(pts)$epsg
#> [1] 4326
# Optional: same sites in tmap (skipped when tmap is not installed)
# tmap::tm_shape(as_sf(sites)) + tmap::tm_dots(col = "elevation")
# Optional: leaflet (skipped when leaflet is not installed)
# leaflet::leaflet(as_sf(sites)) |>
#   leaflet::addTiles() |>
#   leaflet::addCircleMarkers()
